doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: The early 1950s album with Ken Hanna
summary: He had many solos on an album with Ken Hanna's good local band, and only later learned Hanna had arranged for Stan Kenton.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me ask you about some of the records you’ve been on. Early 50s, with Ken Hanna?

Yes I did an album with Ken Hanna had quite a few solos actually to play on that album, and that was a good band, a local band. It never went anywhere. I think Ken was a — I © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

learned this after I was on the band — that he had been an arranger for Stan Kenton, which I didn’t know until afterwards. But that was a good band. That’s a pretty good album. Every ten, fifteen years I may get it out and play it again.
Yeah. Check it out. See if it’s holding up.
